# Security, Integration and Operations Checklist: Central Authentication and Authorization Service

**Purpose**: Validate that the specification, plan and contracts define security, consumer-integration and operational requirements completely, clearly and consistently before task generation
**Created**: 2026-10-02
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md), [contracts/](../contracts/)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Depth / audience**: formal pre-implementation gate for the author and a PR reviewer. Items evaluate what is written, not whether code works. Certificate items apply because the clarification permits (but does not require) X.509; the plan supports both PEM and PFX sources.

## Authentication Requirements

- [ ] CHK001 Is the email login identifier defined precisely (format validation, case-insensitivity, normalization, maximum length)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, Edge Cases] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: format-validation rule and maximum length are not defined (case-insensitivity is: Spec Edge Cases); Identity's default email validation applies and should be set explicitly during implementation.
- [x] CHK002 Is "indistinguishable" failure defined with a measurable standard for body, status and timing, rather than "as far as practical"? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005, SC-002] Evidence: Spec FR-005 (identical status code and body; password-verification work for an unknown email; no tighter timing guarantee), SC-002.
- [x] CHK003 Are the non-credential failure paths (malformed email, missing fields, rate-limit 429, lockout) specified so that none reveals account existence? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Contracts §login] Evidence: Spec Edge Cases (validation errors reveal nothing about existence), FR-005 (lockout uses the same generic failure), FR-021 (429 is per source address only); Contracts http-api §login (400/401/429).
- [x] CHK004 Is the externally visible behavior of lockout defined consistently between the spec's "throttle" and the plan's 5-failure/15-minute lockout? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021, Plan §R5] Evidence: Spec FR-021 (5 failures, 15 minutes, same generic failure as FR-005) matches Plan R5 and Plan Key Design (Throttling).
- [x] CHK005 Are throttle thresholds (attempts, window, scope per account vs per source) quantified in a requirement rather than left to implementation? [Gap, Spec §FR-021] Evidence: Spec FR-021 (5 attempts/15 min per account; 10 requests/min per source; all configurable).
- [x] CHK006 Is disabled-user behavior specified for every entry point: login, refresh, reset-code redemption, and tokens already issued? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006, Assumptions] Evidence: Spec FR-014 and Clarifications (checklist resolution) (an Administrator may issue a code for a disabled account; redemption fails while it is disabled with the same generic failure as an invalid code, revealing no state; a failed redemption does not consume the code; re-enabling does not sign the user in; session and access-token rules unchanged), US3 scenario 10; Contracts http-api §reset-password (401 same response) and §password-reset; Research R6 (disabled accounts).
- [x] CHK007 Is the acceptable lag between disabling a user and consumer APIs rejecting that user's existing access token stated as a measurable bound (the token lifetime)? [Measurability, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-007] Evidence: Spec Assumptions (changes reach consumers when the access token expires), Edge Cases, FR-007 (15 min default, range 1-60).
- [ ] CHK008 Does the spec list everything that must never expose passwords (responses, logs, errors, token claims, documentation examples) rather than only responses and logs? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: FR-015, FR-007 (exact claims), FR-014, FR-031 and FR-024 cover responses, logs, tokens and documentation in effect, but validation error text and documentation examples are not named explicitly.
- [x] CHK009 Are requirements for other secrets that must stay out of logs (access tokens, refresh tokens, reset codes, key material, bootstrap password) stated in the spec, not only in the constitution and plan? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, FR-015] Evidence: Spec FR-031 (passwords, access tokens, refresh tokens, reset codes and key material never logged), FR-009.
- [x] CHK010 Is the password rule stated in one authoritative place and applied consistently to creation, reset and bootstrap? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, §FR-019] Evidence: Domain PasswordPolicy is the single source (Plan Key Design: Password rule; Research R6); applied to creation and reset (Spec FR-015) and to bootstrap (Plan Key Design: Bootstrap; Research R7; Spec FR-026).
- [x] CHK011 Is the requirement for transport security (HTTPS/TLS termination) for credentials and tokens in transit defined, or explicitly assigned to the deployment environment? [Gap] Evidence: Spec Clarifications 2026-10-02 (analysis remediation), TLS bullet; Assumptions (TLS-terminating reverse proxy).
- [x] CHK012 Is the trust level of an Administrator in the reset workflow stated, given that a reset code lets the issuing Administrator set the user's password and sign in as them? [Gap, Assumption, Spec §FR-014] Evidence: Spec Assumptions (Administrators are trusted accounts; a reset code allows account takeover) and Clarifications.

## Authorization Requirements

- [x] CHK013 Is the role set stated identically (names, spelling, case) in the spec, constitution, plan and contracts? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, Plan §Data Model] Evidence: Spec FR-002, Constitution IV, Data Model §Role, Contracts http-api (Administrator | Manager | Operator, same spelling and case).
- [ ] CHK014 Is the behavior of role-name matching defined (case-sensitive, exact) for the role route value and role arrays in requests? [Clarity, Contracts §user administration] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: Contracts say role values are 'validated against' the three names; exact, case-sensitive matching is stated only in tasks.
- [x] CHK015 Is each Administrator-only operation enumerated so no administration endpoint is ambiguous (including password reset issuance)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012, Contracts §User administration] Evidence: Spec FR-012, FR-014; Contracts http-api §User administration lists every /api/users route, including password-reset, under the Administrator policy.
- [x] CHK016 Is the status code distinction between unauthenticated (401) and unauthorized (403) specified for administration endpoints in the spec, not only in the contract? [Gap, Spec §FR-012, Contracts] Evidence: Spec US2 scenario 3 (no or invalid token is unauthenticated), US2 scenario 2 and US3 scenario 6 (Manager/Operator are forbidden).
- [x] CHK017 Are the rules protecting the system from lockout (last enabled Administrator, last remaining role) complete for every operation that can change those states, including self-modification? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020, Edge Cases] Evidence: Spec FR-020 and Edge Cases (changes leaving no enabled Administrator or a role-less user are refused); covers disable and role removal.
- [ ] CHK018 Is the requirement that role information from clients is never trusted stated with concrete cases (create user request, role assignment, token claims presented to the service)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: FR-013 is generic; the concrete cases are covered by FR-002, FR-008 and FR-012 but not enumerated.
- [ ] CHK019 Are the consumer API authorization expectations specified (what a consumer must check, how roles map to claims, how multiple roles are treated, what Manager/Operator may do in consumers)? [Completeness, Spec §Authorization, FR-030] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: claim mapping, validation parameters and multi-role handling are in the contract; what Manager and Operator may do inside a consumer is not stated (see CHK021).
- [x] CHK020 Does the spec define the rejection outcome for unsupported roles in every place a role can enter (assignment, user creation, route value)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-002, Contracts] Evidence: Spec FR-002, US3 scenario 5, SC-005; Contracts http-api (create user 400, PUT/DELETE role 400).
- [ ] CHK021 Is the intended relationship between Manager and Operator privileges defined, or explicitly left to each consumer API? [Ambiguity, Spec §Roles] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: nothing says Manager and Operator privileges are defined by each consumer API; a one-line assumption or documentation statement is needed.

## Token and Key Requirements

- [x] CHK022 Is the token authority boundary stated: what this service signs, what consumers must verify, and that consumers never call this service per request? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, §Consumer API Independence] Evidence: Spec FR-008, FR-009, Key Entities (Signing Key Pair, Consumer API).
- [x] CHK023 Is the issuer value defined as a configurable requirement with rules for consumers to match it exactly? [Gap, Spec §FR-007, Contracts §token] Evidence: Spec FR-007 (iss), FR-026 (issuer is mandatory configuration), SC-003 (wrong issuer rejected); Contracts token-and-jwks (consumers MUST check iss).
- [x] CHK024 Is the audience model defined (one shared audience versus one per consumer API), including how a new consumer API is added without reissuing tokens? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007, FR-030] Evidence: Contracts token-and-jwks (aud is one configured audience shared by consumer APIs); Spec FR-030 (a new consumer needs only consumer-side configuration).
- [x] CHK025 Is the access-token lifetime stated as a requirement with allowed configuration range and the permitted clock skew for consumers? [Measurability, Spec §FR-007, Contracts §token] Evidence: Spec FR-007 (default 15, range 1-60); Contracts token-and-jwks (clock skew at most 1 minute).
- [x] CHK026 Is the minimum claim set consistent across the spec, research and contract (sub, role, iss, aud, exp, plus iat/nbf/jti), and is the exclusion of email stated as a requirement? [Consistency, Spec §Authorization, Plan §R3] Evidence: Spec FR-007 (exactly sub, role, iss, aud, iat, exp; no other claims, so no email), Research R3, Contracts token-and-jwks, Plan Summary.
- [x] CHK027 Is the claim shape for roles unambiguous when a user holds one role versus several? [Clarity, Contracts §token] Evidence: Contracts token-and-jwks (one role claim per role; JSON array when several).
- [x] CHK028 Is the asymmetric algorithm and minimum key strength stated as a requirement, including rejection of weaker keys at startup? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, Plan §R1, §R11] Evidence: Spec FR-009 (asymmetric); Research R1 (RS256, RSA at least 2048 bits) and R11 (weaker keys rejected at startup).
- [x] CHK029 Are private and public signing material separated in requirements for every artifact (image, repository, logs, JWKS, documentation, consumer configuration)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009, Constitution §V] Evidence: Spec FR-009 (never exposed to consumers, logs, documentation); Constitution V; Research R12 (never copied into an image, read-only secret mount); Contracts JWKS (no private parameters).
- [x] CHK030 Are consumer requirements for validating tokens stated so that no database access, password data or service call is needed, including the failure behavior when the key source is unreachable? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, Edge Cases] Evidence: Spec FR-008, FR-010, Clarifications (keep last fetched keys; fail closed if none); Contracts token-and-jwks §Consumer key-retrieval behavior.
- [x] CHK031 Is the requirement that refresh tokens must never be accepted by consumer APIs stated? [Gap, Contracts §Refresh token] Evidence: Contracts token-and-jwks §Refresh token (never accepted by consumer APIs; opaque, not a JWT).

## Certificate and Key Management Requirements (X.509 permitted)

- [x] CHK032 Are requirements for handling the private certificate or key defined end to end (provisioning, storage permissions, who can read it, password handling)? [Completeness, Plan §R1, Spec §FR-009] Evidence: Spec FR-034 (readable only by the service process and the provisioning identity; ownership and permissions block unrelated users and processes; read-only mount where practical; never in an image or repository; no consumer access; PFX password only from external secret configuration and never in source control, Dockerfiles, literal Compose values, logs or generated documentation; missing or invalid PFX credentials fail Production startup clearly; PEM follows equivalent rules; throwaway local validation keys exempt); Plan Key Design (Signing-key protection: owner operator, group runtime GID, mode 0640, directory 0750); Research R1, R11.
- [x] CHK033 Is public certificate/key distribution specified, including whether consumers must use the JWKS endpoint, a static file, or either, and who updates them on rotation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, Contracts §JWKS] Evidence: Contracts token-and-jwks §JWKS and §Alternative distribution (JWKS or static public key; a static-key consumer must update on rotation).
- [x] CHK034 Are certificate/key expiration requirements defined (behavior when the signing certificate is expired or near expiry, and whether the service fails, warns or continues)? [Gap, Spec §FR-010] Evidence: Spec FR-010 and Clarifications (validity dates not enforced; expiry logged at startup; operators rotate before expiry), FR-031.
- [x] CHK035 Is the rotation procedure defined with measurable overlap rules (minimum overlap equals token lifetime plus skew) and a defined effect on in-flight tokens? [Measurability, Spec §Edge Cases, Contracts §Rotation] Evidence: Contracts token-and-jwks §Rotation contract (remove old key after at least one token lifetime plus skew); Spec Edge Cases (tokens signed by the previous key stay valid during the overlap).
- [x] CHK036 Is the key identifier strategy defined as a requirement (what `kid` is derived from, who consumes it, behavior of a consumer that sees an unknown `kid`)? [Gap, Plan §R1, Contracts §token] Evidence: Research R1 (kid is the base64url SHA-256 thumbprint of the public key); Contracts token-and-jwks (consumers resolve by kid; an unknown kid triggers a key refresh).
- [x] CHK037 Is emergency key replacement (suspected compromise) specified, including whether tokens signed by the old key are rejected immediately? [Gap, Recovery] Evidence: Spec FR-035 and Clarifications (checklist resolution) (emergency replacement differs from rotation; compromised key stops signing immediately; public key removed from publication as soon as operationally possible with no overlap; JWKS consumers replace their cached set and drop it within 5 minutes; static-key consumers keep accepting it until updated, a limitation the documentation must state; trust in the old key outranks already-issued tokens; tokens signed with it are untrusted once consumers are updated; sessions not destroyed automatically; no revocation service or introspection); Contracts token-and-jwks §Emergency key replacement; Plan Key Design; Research R2.
- [ ] CHK038 Is the publication scope of the JWKS endpoint (anonymous, cacheable, public-only parameters) required rather than only described in the contract? [Gap, Spec §FR-010] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: public-only content is required (FR-009) and cacheability is in the contract, but anonymous access to the key endpoint is not a stated requirement.

## Session Renewal Requirements

- [x] CHK039 Are the refresh-token lifetime and whether it is absolute or sliding stated unambiguously? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016, Clarifications] Evidence: Spec FR-016 and Clarifications (checklist resolution) (individual lifetime 7 days by default, fresh on rotation; absolute session lifetime 30 days by default from the original sign-in; rotation cannot extend it; sign in again at the cap; both configurable, validated at startup, absolute >= individual), US4 scenarios 5-6; Data Model RefreshToken (SessionStartedAt, SessionExpiresAt, capped ExpiresAt); Research R4, R11; Contracts http-api §refresh.
- [x] CHK040 Is the persistence requirement for refresh tokens stated precisely (non-recoverable form, uniqueness, minimum entropy) in the spec and not only in the plan? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016, Plan §R4] Evidence: Spec FR-016 (opaque, stored only in non-recoverable form); Research R4 (32 random bytes, SHA-256 hash); Data Model RefreshToken (unique TokenHash).
- [ ] CHK041 Is the retention and cleanup of expired, rotated and revoked token records specified, given that reuse detection depends on keeping them? [Gap, Plan §R4] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: Data Model and Research R4 keep rows until expiry plus a 'documented cleanup', but no cleanup procedure or documentation task exists.
- [x] CHK042 Is behavior for two concurrent renewals with the same token defined, including the user-visible outcome? [Edge Case, Plan §R4] Evidence: Research R4 Concurrency (the second request sees Rotated, the family is revoked; a client racing itself is signed out).
- [x] CHK043 Is the definition of "session" (token family) and the scope of revocation consistent across logout, reuse detection, disable and reset? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017, FR-018, FR-014] Evidence: Spec FR-014, FR-017, FR-018; Data Model RefreshToken (family and per-user revocation); Plan Key Design (Refresh tokens).
- [x] CHK044 Is reuse-detection behavior fully specified, including which tokens become invalid and what the legitimate user must do next? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017, User Story 4] Evidence: Spec FR-017 and US4 scenario 2 (rejected; the entire session including its latest refresh token is revoked). The next step for the legitimate user is a fresh sign-in (FR-003); implied rather than stated, accepted.
- [ ] CHK045 Are logout semantics defined for edge inputs (unknown, expired or already revoked token, missing body) and for idempotency? [Coverage, Spec §FR-018, Contracts §logout] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: Contracts cover unknown tokens (204, idempotent); expired or revoked tokens and a missing body are not specified.
- [x] CHK046 Does the spec state whether an administrator disabling or resetting a user must immediately stop renewal, as distinct from existing access tokens? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, FR-018] Evidence: Spec FR-006, FR-014, FR-018 (sessions revoked immediately on disable and reset); Assumptions (existing access tokens live until expiry).

## Initial Administrator Requirements

- [ ] CHK047 Are the exact bootstrap preconditions defined (zero users, configuration present) including the case where the store is empty but configuration is missing in Development versus Production? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019, User Story 6] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: Production behavior is defined (FR-019, FR-026); Development behavior with an empty store and no bootstrap configuration is not.
- [x] CHK048 Is the mechanism for becoming unavailable defined and objectively verifiable by an operator (observable signal after the first user exists)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-019, Plan §R7] Evidence: Spec FR-019 (configuration ignored once any user exists); Research R7 (log line 'Bootstrap skipped: users already exist'; restart with different values).
- [x] CHK049 Is atomicity of bootstrap specified (creating the user and assigning the Administrator role succeed or fail together, and a failed run is safely retried)? [Gap, Plan §R7] Evidence: Research R7 and Plan Key Design (IUserCreator writes user and role in one transaction; the store stays empty on failure, so retry is safe).
- [x] CHK050 Is the handling of the bootstrap secret defined (how supplied, when to remove, not logged, not stored)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019, Plan §R7] Evidence: Spec FR-019 (externally supplied configuration; documentation advises removal), FR-031 (passwords never logged); Plan Key Design (Bootstrap__AdminPassword).
- [x] CHK051 Is behavior defined for the corner case where all users have been removed from a previously initialized store, and is it intended to reopen bootstrap? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-019] Evidence: Spec FR-019 (allowed whenever the store contains no users) and FR-012 (no user-deletion operation), so reopening is by definition and reachable only by manual database changes.

## Persistence and Data Preservation Requirements

- [x] CHK052 Is durability of the SQLite data across container replacement stated as a testable requirement, including which paths must live on persistent storage (database and data-protection keys)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-025, Plan §R6, §R8] Evidence: Spec FR-025, Edge Cases (restart or redeploy keeps users, roles, sessions); Plan Technical Context Storage (database and data-protection keys on a named volume); Quickstart §6.
- [x] CHK053 Is the dependency of password-reset validity on persisted data-protection keys captured in a requirement and in backup scope? [Gap, Plan §R6] Evidence: Plan Technical Context Storage and Research R6 (a lost key ring invalidates outstanding reset codes); Quickstart §8 (backup includes /data/keys).
- [ ] CHK054 Are requirements for applying migrations defined for clean install, upgrade, and failure (partial migration, rollback or restore path)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-025, Plan §R8] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: clean install and upgrade are defined (Research R8); behavior after a failed or partial migration (restore from backup) is not stated.
- [ ] CHK055 Is a policy defined for destructive or irreversible migrations and for downgrades? [Gap] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: no policy for irreversible migrations or downgrades; not needed for the initial schema.
- [x] CHK056 Is "production startup never deletes or resets data" expressed as an observable requirement covering migration, bootstrap and test code paths? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025, Constitution §VI] Evidence: Spec FR-025, FR-019; Constitution VI; Research R8 (no EnsureCreated, no automatic destructive action).
- [ ] CHK057 Are concurrency and single-writer expectations for SQLite stated (single instance only, behavior if two instances share the volume)? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: single node is stated (Assumptions, Plan Technical Context); behavior if two instances share the volume is not.

## Containerized Development Requirements

- [x] CHK058 Is the prohibition on installing .NET or project tooling in the agent container stated as a requirement with an unambiguous scope (SDK, EF tools, SQLite tools)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-028, Constitution §IX] Evidence: Spec FR-028; Constitution IX (no .NET SDK, ASP.NET tooling, EF tooling, SQLite tooling or project runtime dependencies in the agent container).
- [x] CHK059 Are the requirements for creating and using the dev environment through the host Docker daemon defined, including how repository files reach containers when the agent itself runs in a container? [Gap, Spec §FR-028, Plan §R12] Evidence: Plan Constitution Check IX/X; Research R12, R14 (dev services use the host daemon; HOST_PROJECT_DIR is the repository path as the host sees it).
- [x] CHK060 Is it specified how bind-mounted paths resolve when Compose is invoked from a container against the host daemon, since volume sources are interpreted by the host? [Gap, Risk, Plan §R12] Evidence: Research R14 and Plan Constitution Check X (HOST_PROJECT_DIR required, fail-fast; no relative host paths; no published ports used from the agent).
- [x] CHK061 Are restore, build, test, migration creation and migration application each covered by a documented Docker-based command requirement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-028, Quickstart] Evidence: Spec FR-028; Quickstart §1-2 (restore, build, test, ef migrations add, migrate service).
- [ ] CHK062 Is the complete list of host prerequisites (Docker version, Compose v2, permissions, network access for package restore, writable cache volumes) stated so none is undocumented? [Completeness, Spec §FR-027, FR-028] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: Quickstart lists Docker, Compose v2 and .env; permissions, network access for package restore and cache volumes are not enumerated.
- [x] CHK063 Is the container health-check approach defined given the runtime image may not contain an HTTP client? [Ambiguity, Plan §R12] Evidence: Research R12 (--healthcheck switch of the published app because the runtime image has no curl).

## Production Documentation Requirements

- [x] CHK064 Is "readable but not interactive" defined with an objective acceptance criterion (what must be absent: send button, server URL, credential input, proxy)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-024, SC-008] Evidence: Research R9 (objective acceptance: no send/execute control, no server URL, no credential input); Spec FR-024, SC-008; Quickstart §9.
- [x] CHK065 Is the verification method for read-only production behavior specified, given the plan could not confirm the Scalar option and lists three fallbacks? [Ambiguity, Plan §R9] Evidence: Research R9 (mandatory smoke check on the production page; three ordered fallbacks; Constitution VIII allows an equivalent configuration). The mechanism is chosen at implementation by inspecting the package, but the outcome is objectively verifiable. WATCH ITEM.
- [ ] CHK066 Is the exposure decision for production documentation stated (anonymous access to the API surface description is accepted, or access is restricted)? [Assumption, Gap, Spec §FR-024] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: production documentation is readable (FR-024) but anonymous exposure of the API description is not stated as accepted; restricting it in the reverse proxy is a deployment choice.
- [x] CHK067 Is the content that must never appear in production documentation listed (example tokens, internal URLs, configuration values, key material)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-024] Evidence: Research R9 (no secrets, example tokens or internal URLs in the production OpenAPI document); Spec FR-009 (no key material in documentation), FR-024.

## Operations and Integration Requirements

- [ ] CHK068 Are the configuration items listed as requirements with required/optional status, defaults and failure behavior, and are production-fatal misconfigurations enumerated? [Completeness, Spec §FR-026, FR-027, Plan §R11] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: production-fatal items are in FR-026 and Research R11; no consolidated configuration requirement (required or optional, defaults) exists yet; the documentation task will provide it.
- [ ] CHK069 Are backup and restore requirements specific on consistency (service stopped versus online), scope (database, key ring, signing key custody) and a recovery success measure? [Clarity, Spec §FR-027, SC-012] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: success measure (SC-012) and options (stop-and-copy or sqlite3 .backup, Research R8) exist; backup scope for signing-key custody is not defined.
- [ ] CHK070 Is the set of "common authentication failures" for troubleshooting enumerated, so documentation completeness can be judged? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-027] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: FR-027 does not enumerate the common failures; only the documentation task does.
- [ ] CHK071 Are consumer integration requirements complete for configuration inputs, required validation parameters, role policies for Administrator, Manager and Operator, and rotation handling? [Completeness, Spec §FR-030, SC-011] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: validation parameters and rotation handling are in the contract; per-role policy examples exist only in the documentation task.
- [x] CHK072 Is a security-relevant event logging requirement defined (what is recorded for failed sign-ins, reuse detection, role changes, bootstrap) without recording secrets? [Gap, Spec §FR-015] Evidence: Spec FR-031 (events listed; no secrets).
- [x] CHK073 Are CORS requirements (allowed frontend origins, production defaults) captured in the spec, since the shared frontend is a stated client? [Gap, Plan §R10] Evidence: Spec FR-032 (origins externally configured; no cross-origin access in production unless configured).
- [x] CHK074 Are health-check requirements specific about what the endpoint may and may not reveal? [Clarity, Plan §R10, Contracts §Health] Evidence: Spec FR-033; Contracts http-api (200 Healthy or 503 Unhealthy, no further detail).
- [ ] CHK075 Are availability and recovery expectations (recovery time, acceptable downtime during key rotation or migration) stated or explicitly excluded? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions] OPEN [ACCEPTABLE DEFERRED]: high availability is excluded (Assumptions); recovery time and downtime during rotation or migration are not stated.
